event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: The filing, dated February 10 2021, repeatedly links the COVID-19 pandemic to both realized and continuing operational, financial and strategic risks for APH.  The company discloses that COVID-19 has already shut plants, constrained suppliers, disrupted logistics, reduced demand and forced large-scale remote-work arrangements in 2020; these are direct, current impacts rather than hypothetical possibilities.  Management further warns that such disruptions are persisting into 2021 and could last “beyond,” amplifying other risk factors (supply-chain volatility, cybersecurity, raw-material sourcing, labour health).  Although no dollar amounts are provided, the language is strong (“material and adverse effect,” “widespread disruptions,” “impossible to predict”) and the breadth of affected areas is global, touching 71 % of sales outside the U.S.  Because the disclosure is within a year of the WHO declaration (March 2020), the Time Decay Principle allows high scores (7-10) for the most concrete, realized impacts, with moderately lower scores (4-6) for generic or heavily qualified statements and very low scores (≤2) where mitigation dominates.  This framework guides the micro-scores below.

evidence_list.snippet: We face significant risks related to adverse public health developments, including epidemics and pandemics such as the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Explicitly acknowledges the firm faces 'significant risks'.
Names the specific event (COVID-19 pandemic).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Sentence establishes a direct risk nexus to COVID-19 but remains generic and unquantified, warranting a mid-level score of 5.

evidence_list.snippet: Any outbreaks of contagious diseases and other adverse public health developments in countries where we operate could have a material and adverse effect on our business, financial condition, liquidity and results of operations.

components.reason: Uses strong wording 'material and adverse effect' across multiple financial dimensions.
Applies globally to all operating countries, broadening exposure.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highlights potential material harm across all key financial metrics; slightly stronger than generic risk, earning 6.

evidence_list.snippet: For example, the COVID-19 pandemic has affected our manufacturing facilities throughout the world, as well as the facilities of our suppliers, customers and our customers’ contract manufacturers.

components.reason: Describes realized (past and ongoing) impacts ('has affected').
Covers entire value chain—internal plants, suppliers, customers.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides concrete evidence of global, multi-tier disruption already occurring; high severity justified.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic has caused widespread disruptions to our Company throughout most of 2020, particularly during the first half of the year.

components.reason: States ‘widespread disruptions’ across the company.
Confirms the duration (most of 2020), demonstrating sustained impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Past, company-wide disruption over an extended period signals high operational risk, scoring 6.

evidence_list.snippet: During the first quarter of 2020, these disruptions were primarily limited to our operations in China, which were closed for three weeks during January and February due to government mandates.

components.reason: Specifies complete plant closures (‘closed for three weeks’)—a hard operational hit.
Quantifies the duration (three weeks), increasing concreteness.
Describes limitation to China only, partially containing scope.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: While the closure is concrete, it was short and geographically bounded, yielding a moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: As the virus spread to the rest of the world beginning in March and continuing throughout the remainder of 2020, most of our other operations outside of China were also impacted.

components.reason: Shows escalation from regional to global impact.
Indicates ongoing effect ‘throughout the remainder of 2020’.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Demonstrates broadening operational disruption, but without quantification; score set at 5.

evidence_list.snippet: As of December 31, 2020, we continue to experience some disruptions, and at a minimum, we expect those disruptions to continue through the first half of 2021 and they could, potentially, extend for the full year and beyond.

components.reason: Confirms ongoing disruptions at the filing date (current impact).
Projects risk into the future (through 2021 and beyond).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Signals sustained, forward-looking risk, meriting a solid mid-range score.

evidence_list.snippet: These disruptions have included and may continue to include, depending on the specific location, government regulations that limit our ability to operate certain of our facilities at full capacity and to adjust certain costs, travel restrictions, “work-from-home” orders, supplier constraints, supply-chain interruptions, logistics challenges and limitations, and reduced demand from certain customers.

components.reason: Enumerates multiple operational pain points (facility capacity, supply chain, demand).
Covers both current and prospective impacts (‘have included and may continue’).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Detailed list of concrete disruptions across operations and demand elevates severity to 6.

evidence_list.snippet: The extent to which the COVID-19 pandemic will continue to impact our business and financial results going forward will be dependent on future developments such as the length and severity of the crisis, future government regulations and actions in response to the crisis, the timing, availability and effectiveness of vaccines, some of which have recently been approved and distributed for use, and the overall impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the global economy and capital markets, among many other factors, all of which remain highly uncertain and unpredictable.

components.reason: Highlights high uncertainty and multiple external variables.
Explicitly ties uncertainty to ongoing financial impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Focuses on unpredictability rather than realized damage, resulting in a moderate-low score of 4.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, the COVID-19 pandemic could impact the health of our management team and other employees.

components.reason: Identifies human-capital risk (executive and workforce health).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Acknowledges a specific but unquantified personnel risk; limited scope yields a low score.

evidence_list.snippet: It is impossible to predict the overall future impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on our business, financial condition, liquidity and financial results, and there can be no assurance that the COVID-19 pandemic will not have a material and adverse effect on our financial results in the future during any quarter or period in which we are affected.

components.reason: Emphasises inability to predict combined with potential material adverse effects.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Strong cautionary language but still hypothetical; moderate score of 3.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, the COVID-19 pandemic increases the likelihood and potential severity of other risks (including some discussed separately within this Item 1A. Risk Factors ), including but not limited to, the following:

components.reason: Shows compounding effect—pandemic exacerbates other risk factors.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Links COVID-19 to amplified overall risk landscape; no specifics, so score kept at 3.

evidence_list.snippet: For example, the COVID-19 pandemic initially disrupted the supply of raw materials, primarily in the first half of 2020; reoccurrences of such unforeseen events may result in the Company experiencing difficulties in obtaining a consistent supply of materials at stable pricing levels.

components.reason: Cites concrete past supply-chain disruption.
Flags potential recurrence affecting material availability and pricing.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific to raw-material sourcing; tangible but narrower in scope, scoring 4.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic may increase our susceptibility to cybersecurity incidents and risks, especially as certain of our employees have transitioned and continue to work from home.

components.reason: Introduces secondary risk pathway (cybersecurity) arising from remote work.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Identifies a derivative risk with limited detail; low severity score of 2.

evidence_list.snippet: During the fourth quarter of 2020 and into 2021, in several regions around the world, including the United States and Europe, there has been a resurgence in COVID-19 cases.

components.reason: Highlights resurgence, signalling renewed operational risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Notes uptick in cases but does not quantify impact; earns a small score.

evidence_list.snippet: The Company continues taking actions to mitigate, as best we can, the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the health and well-being of our employees, the communities in which we operate and our partners, as well as the impact on our operations and business as a whole.

components.reason: Describes mitigation efforts, reducing net risk perception.
Acknowledges ongoing impact requiring mitigation.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Sentence focuses on mitigation; net effect is a reduction of perceived risk, resulting in a negative contribution.

evidence_list.snippet: However, there can be no assurance that the COVID-19 pandemic will not have a material and adverse impact on our operations, financial condition, liquidity and results of operations.

components.reason: Admits possibility of material adverse impact across multiple financial areas.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: A cautionary statement of potential severity without detail; moderate score of 3.
